items.title: How much do N future changes actually cost, at different coupling penalties?
items.description: Grounded in L3's notification-channel example: each new channel costs the same as the last under the decoupled design (0% coupling penalty), but compounds under the coupled design because every addition means editing OrderService itself and reasoning about its growing branches. Set the coupling penalty to 0% to reproduce the flat, decoupled cost from L3. Push it up to 15% (the default, representing the coupled version) or higher to see how fast a small per-change penalty compounds once you're past a handful of changes — drag the number of changes out past 10 or 15 to see where the two designs really diverge.

params.name: baseCostPerChange
params.label: Hours to build the first channel

params.name: couplingPenaltyPercent
params.label: Cost growth per additional channel (coupling penalty)

items.compute: const growth = params.couplingPenaltyPercent / 100; let cumulative = 0; let costOfChange = params.baseCostPerChange; for (let i = 0; i < params.numChanges; i++) { cumulative += costOfChange; costOfChange *= (1 + growth); } return { cumulativeCost: Math.round(cumulative * 100) / 100 };
